questions.question: What can chromatography be used for besides analysis?
options: Separating large kilograms of industrial waste
Both separation of minute samples and analysis
Determining the magnetism of metals
Filtering out large rocks from water

questions.question: If a substance is pure, how many spots will it produce on a chromatogram?
options: No spots at all
Only one spot
At least three spots
Many different spots

questions.question: What will a mixture produce when analysed using paper chromatography?
options: A single spot
No spots
Many spots
A straight line of pencil

questions.question: Why is a pencil used to draw the starting line in paper chromatography?
options: Pencil is insoluble in water
Pencil dissolves quickly in water
Pencil reacts chemically with the ink
Pencil ink travels faster than the solvent

questions.question: When is simple distillation specifically used instead of fractional distillation?
options: To separate a mixture containing only two substances
To separate a mixture of four or more gases
To separate substances with identical boiling points
To separate magnetic solids from liquids

questions.question: In which scenario is fractional distillation most appropriate?
options: Separating insoluble sand from water
Separating mixtures with 3 or more substances, or those with similar boiling points
Separating a single pure solute from its crystal form
Separating magnetic iron filings from non-magnetic sulfur

questions.question: What happens during distillation if the condenser warms up?
options: It becomes more effective and condenses gas faster
The boiling point of the mixture increases
It becomes less effective and more gas will escape
It filters out fine particles more efficiently

questions.question: How can you obtain larger crystals during the process of crystallisation?
options: By boiling the solution rapidly
By allowing the solvent to evaporate more slowly
By adding a chemical catalyst
By freezing the solution instantly

questions.question: Which materials can be separated from a mixture using a magnet?
options: Copper and brass
Aluminium and gold
Iron and steel
Lead and zinc

questions.question: What process is used to separate insoluble solids from a liquid using a filter?
options: Crystallisation
Filtration
Simple distillation
Chromatography

questions.question: What is the purpose of placing a drop of water on the filter funnel when setting up filter paper?
options: To dissolve the solid mixture beforehand
To speed up the evaporation of the solvent
To help keep the filter paper cone open for easy filtering
To neutralise any acidic particles in the mixture

questions.question: What happens if immiscible liquids are mixed and then allowed to settle?
options: They form a perfectly uniform single solution
They do not mix and one will float above the other
They react chemically to form a solid precipitate
They instantly evaporate into the air

questions.question: What occurs if miscible liquids are left standing together in a container?
options: They separate into distinct layers based on density
They do not separate into layers
They instantly crystallise into a solid
They form a visible boundary line in the middle

questions.question: What sequence of techniques is needed to separate pure salt from rock salt?
options: Making a solution, filtration, and crystallisation
Simple distillation, chromatography, and magnetism
Decanting, fractional distillation, and evaporation
Making a solution, fractional distillation, and paper chromatography

questions.question: Why must a condenser be kept cold during the distillation process?
options: To prevent the liquid from boiling too quickly
To speed up condensation
To allow insoluble solids to settle
To make the solute evaporate faster

questions.question: What can be said about the purity of the liquid collected (distillate) after distillation?
options: It is a concentrated mixture
It contains highly insoluble impurities
The liquid collected (distillate) is pure
It is an unsaturated solution of salt
